en: There is a city in the world known as Avarṣi, where Kātyāyanī reigns;
her grace is that very genius which, celebrated here as "Geya," triumphs in Chatrapurī. 1.

You alone appear distinct from her; you are radiant, like a lamp to the wick of a lamp. O Kātyāyanī, you are the remover of the suffering of those who take refuge in you, the one with purified limbs, and the bestower of wisdom. || 2 ||
O Goddess, you are here known as Gaṇapati, attended by Brahmā, Uruvetālaka, Siṃha, Dāḍha, Subhairava, and those named the Agni-gaṇas, together with your own hosts.

O Giver of Boons, salutations to You, who are to be served by the Brahmins born of the lineages of Jamadagni, Bhāradvāja, Atri, Kaśyapa, and Kauśika, as well as those born of the families of Kauṇḍinya and Vatsa.
I worship you, who have been consecrated with cow’s milk, who wear red garments and are anointed with red sandalwood;
you who are beautified by auspicious garlands of *bilva* leaves, who delight in edible offerings, and for whom rows of lamps are dear to your heart.

O Goddess, slayer of the demon Mahisha, who holds in Your hands the sword, the conch, the tail of the demon Mahishasura, and the trident thrust into the mouth of Mahishasura, protect me day and night.

O Victorious One, O Refuge, O You of lightning-like luster, who bears upon Your head the jewel-encrusted golden crown named Bāṇeśvara-liṅga situated at Your own peak—conquer, and make me victorious! 7.

O Mother Yaśodā, who reside on the right side of Netrāvatī, who are served by Vidyādharas and hosts of Nāgas, who are a mass of compassion, grant us eternal bliss; O giver of auspiciousness, O you of beautiful eyes!
Whoever recites with devotion this "Eight Verses on the Grace of Goddess Kātyāyanī," which was composed by Kumaṭhācārya and bestows desired boons, shall become happy. (9)
Thus ends the Śrī Kātyāyanī Aṣṭaka in its entirety.
